jobs.occupation: PhD Researcher (m/f/d) AI for Semantic Structures, Reasoning Flows & Personalized Content Generation (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: Become a part of our journey and join the Constructor Community as:PhD Researcher (m/f/d): AI for Semantic Structures, Reasoning Flows & Personalized Content GenerationYou are expected to contribute to the development of internationally visible, foundational research in AI-driven semantic structure extraction, automated reasoning-flow modeling, and adaptive content generation. The research focuses on methods for analyzing and representing deep semantic and pedagogical structures in scientific and educational materials; high-fidelity extraction of conceptual and reasoning blocks; inference-time rationale generation; and adaptive, learner-aware sequencing of content. This includes work on semantic parsing, structured NLP, graph-based neural models, metacognitive prompting, ontology alignment across disciplines, and human-in-the-loop optimization.In this context, interdisciplinary research is strongly encouraged—particularly collaborations spanning computer science, computational linguistics, cognitive science, and the learning sciences. You will contribute to developing datasets, baseline models, personalized learning engines, reasoning-graph representations, cross-domain mapping algorithms, and RLHF-style feedback loops that improve system interpretability and instructional quality. The successful candidate will also contribute to high-quality publications, release research prototypes, and support demonstrator systems that deliver structured semantic extraction, rationale-aware content generation, and cross-domain transfer of reasoning structures.Additionally, the successful candidate is expected to support teaching activities in areas such as Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, AI in Education, Knowledge Representation, and Python-based analytical seminars at the BSc, MSc, and PhD levels. Responsibilities include assisting in course delivery, advising students, supervising Bachelor/Master theses, and engaging in methodological innovation for online, hybrid, and in-person learning environments. The university provides strong support for early-career researchers, including mentorship, administrative assistance, access to computational resources, conference funding, and opportunities to collaborate with other research groups and industrial partners working at the intersection of AI and digital education.Your Profile- Master’s or PhD degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computational Linguistics, or a related field.- Strong research interest and practical experience in one or more of the following areas: - semantic parsing and structured representation learning- knowledge graphs or graph-based reasoning- transformer models, sequence modeling, or GNNs- natural language generation and explainability- educational AI, personalization algorithms, or cognitive modeling- Evidence of research potential through publications, a strong thesis, or significant projects.- Experience or interest in innovative teaching and learning approaches.- Ability to translate theoretical insights into engineered prototypes and systems supporting scientific or educational use cases.- Responsible, self-motivated, and capable of working independently as well as collaboratively.- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.- Intercultural competence and experience in international environments.- Fluency with co-pilot tools for coding and writing.- Fluency in English, the language of instruction and communication on campus.Funding & Appointment TermsThe appointment provides full financial coverage through a dedicated fellowship, comprising:- Monthly stipend of €1,650- Monthly research-cost allowance of €100 (Forschungskostenpauschale)- Health-insurance subsidy of €100 per month- Supplementary €550 mini-job allowance to support parallel part-time employment (optional)Application Details- Expected start date: February, 2026Application package must include:- Curriculum Vitae (CV)- Academic transcripts- A detailed letter of motivation outlining research interests and career goals- 2 recommendation lettersApplications to be reviewed on a rolling basis. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interviews.

jobs.description: Constructor University (formerly Jacobs University) is a private, state-accredited, English-language university in Bremen. We offer Bachelor, Master, and PhD programs in three schools: School of Science, School of Computer Science and Engineering, and School of Business, Social and Decision Sciences. Our principles are first-class teaching and research, international diversity, and transdisciplinary cooperation. According to the 2024 Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings, Constructor University is among the top 25 percent out of more than 1900 universities worldwide and is ranked as the second most international university in the world. As an international university, we attract highly talented and open-minded students from all over the world. Currently, over 1,600 students from 110 nations live and study on our residential campus.The research group led by Prof. Dr. Andrey Ustyuzhanin at Constructor University, in collaboration with Constructor Knowledge Labs (CKL) and Constructor Technology (industry partner), invites applications for Ph.D. student positions in the field of Computer Science, with a focus on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML).This PhD position is part of an initiative to advance knowledge representation and adaptive reasoning systems. The research will focus on developing flexible frameworks for actionable knowledge representation that support storage, retrieval, and dynamic adaptation of information across diverse tasks.Key objectives include:- Transforming unstructured data into interactive knowledge graphs and personalized cognitive maps.- Designing models that provide interpretable, persistent, and navigable structures of knowledge.- Addressing challenges such as hierarchy, composability, and coarse-graining for robust, task-specific reasoning.- Exploring individual and community-level knowledge modeling, including personalized domain maps, profile extraction from artifacts (e.g., papers, courses), and cross-domain abstraction.The overarching goal is to create systems that enable transparent, adaptive, and spatially intuitive representations of knowledge, supporting both individual users and collaborative communities.Your Profile:- Holding recognized MSc degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, AI, ML, or a related discipline.- Students holding BSc degree and exhibiting outstanding performance and extraordinary potential can apply for fast-track PhD.- Strong mathematical background supported with experience in defining and developing knowledge-graph or information retrieval systems.- Hands-on experience with large language models (LLMs) and their applications.- A track record of publications in AI/ML or related areas.- Documented experience in practical research work.- Strong skills in academic English writing (peer-reviewed papers, reports, or equivalent).Funding & Appointment TermsThe appointment provides full financial coverage through a dedicated fellowship, comprising:- Monthly stipend of €1,650- Monthly research-cost allowance of €100 (Forschungskostenpauschale)- Health-insurance subsidy of €100 per month- Supplementary €550 mini-job allowance to support parallel part-time employment (optional)Application Details- Expected start jobs.occupation: W2 Professorship “Sustainable Freight Transport Systems and Transport Logistics" (Ingenieur/in - Verkehrswesen)
jobs.description: W2 Professorship “Sustainable Freight Transport Systems and Transport Logistics"Application deadline:30.12.2026Date of hire:as soon as possibleVacancy number:39565We are seeking an academically outstanding individual (m/f/d) who will make an independent inter- and transdisciplinary contribution to research in the field of sustainable freight transport systems and logistics. The content focus is at the intersection of value chains, freight transport, and sustainable production systems. The professorship shall connect and strengthen the sustainability-related systems analytical topics at the Kassel Institute for Sustainability and the transportation science topics in the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering. Moreover, there is an aim to foster networking in the fields of supply chains and intralogistics with the relevant departments of Economics and Mechanical Engineering. This is intended to further the interdisciplinary interaction between technical and societal research approaches and to advance the research focus on sustainable transformation at the University of Kassel.The professorship should focus on at least one of the following topics:1. Systemic analysis of the interdependencies between freight transport systems, trade, and economic development: Origin of freight transport, economic and ecological evaluation of interregional division of labor, interactions between infrastructure (e.g., rail), regional production clusters and division of labor, as well as sustainable design of these relationships.2. Modeling of the freight transport system: Development and application of scenarios and models for the origin, development, and management of freight transport, infrastructure development and the associated policy instruments, as well as the advancement of corresponding methods.3. Development and application of comprehensive approaches for sustainability evaluation of the ecological, social, and economic effects of strategies and interventions in freight transport, as well as, based on these, the design of a sustainable freight transport system.Experience in the collection, analysis, and management of data in the context of the transformation towards a sustainable freight transport system is also desirable, including the consideration of AI methods: development of data collection procedures and methods of data analysis and data-driven forecasts based on statistical and AI methods, issues regarding the (public) availability and use of data.In teaching, the professorship should supplement and enhance existing degree programs in the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, and to develop new or emerging study programs with a focus on sustainability. Teaching responsibilities are to be divided, with 50% in sustainability-related degree programs and 50% in offerings within the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering. Some courses must be taught in English. It is expected that the appointee, especially regarding official duties in teaching and academic self-administration, will acquire sufficient proficiency in the German language in due course, if not already possessed.The main location for the professorship will be at the Kassel Institute for Sustainability.Special notes: The department aims to increase the proportion of female professors and expressly encourages female scientists to apply.The requirements for appointment and performance are in accordance with §§ 67, 68 HessHG. Specifically, a completed, qualified doctorate as well as a habilitation or equivalent additional academic achievements, as evidenced by scientific publications, are required. You should also possess pedagogical aptitude and commitment to academic teaching, as well as a pronounced willingness for interdisciplinary collaboration.Please submit a curriculum vitae, certificates, diplomas, a list of scientific works, three selected publications, a research and teaching concept (maximum three pages each), as well as a list of previous courses taught, existing teaching evaluations, and any higher education didactic trainings with your application. Additionally, please submit a brief concept (maximum three pages) outlining your ideas for a professional and institutional connection to the Kassel Institute for Sustainability.For questions, please contact Prof. Dr. Angela Francke, Tel.: +49 561 804-7703, Email: angela.francke(at)uni-kassel.de. We kindly ask you to submit the complete application documents as a single PDF document via the University of Kassel's application portal.

jobs.description: Please note:  Applicants must have the  legal right to work in Germany . This includes holding an appropriate and valid visa if required. SunExpress will not provide relocation assistance- Responsible for the revenue optimization on a portion of SunExpress’ broad flight network- Analyze changes in market conditions such as capacity, competition and demand to develop, implement and track appropriate steering strategies with the objective of achieving and exceeding RASK targets- implement revenue management actions by adjusting dynamic prices and/or availability for seat-only and tour-operator channels- responsible for Business Rule adjustments according to market development- working on monthly forecast figures- Assist in implementing new business process changes as well as projects and reporting- Monitor KPI performance, adjusting and communicating strategies needed to meet goals- Point of contact for our international touroperator partnersIhr Profil:The role requires fluent proficiency of German and English language and strong knowledge in Excel and PowerPoint- Holds a formal job entry qualification, either a degree in Business Administration or a comparable field, or a completed commercial or tourism-related vocational apprenticeship.- For the Junior Analyst level, first professional experience, ideally within the airline or leisure industry.- For the Analyst level, at least three years of relevant professional experience are required, preferably in the airline, tourism or leisure industry.- is number-driven and shows analytical mind-set- comfortably able to deal with uncertain outcomes in a highly complex and rapidly changing environment.- carries the capacity to quickly assess complex tasks and is able to deliver optimal solutions self-sufficiently.- in-depth knowledge of GDS reservation systems is considered as an asset
